candidates.hypothesis: Baseline and round-1 candidates are launch-bound, not bandwidth-bound: ~2.8us per eager elementwise op on an 8192-element tensor. Cutting launches from 4 (round 1) to 3 should remove roughly one fixed dispatch+launch cost from the measured p50, i.e. ~2-3us off the 11.264us reading.
candidates.change: run(inputs) now computes combined = torch.add(x, y, alpha=0.6) (one kernel producing x + 0.6y), then scaled = torch.addcmul(shift, combined, ones, value=1.25) (one kernel producing 1.25*combined - 0.125), then returns scaled.relu_() (one in-place kernel). The -0.125 shift tensor and a ones tensor are cached per (shape, dtype, device) so the hot path allocates only the single output tensor. Algebraically 1.25*(x + 0.6y) - 0.125 == 1.25x + 0.75y - 0.125; 1.25 and 0.125 are exact in fp32, so the only new rounding is the inexact 0.6 alpha (~1.5e-7 absolute at the largest magnitudes here, versus an allowed ~1.1e-4 from atol=1e-5/rtol=1e-5). Inputs x and y are read-only: no in-place op touches them, so repeated correctness and benchmark calls stay pure.

nextAction.title: Measure the 3-launch candidate, then try a single-op fused path if launch count is still the binding cost
nextAction.reason: Round 1 showed correctness passes reliably and that p50 scales with launch count (6 launches/15.36us baseline -> 4 launches/11.264us). This round tests whether a 3-launch eager path scales the same way. The stated target (99.9999% of 15.36us) implies ~1.5e-5us, which no kernel-based implementation can reach, so the practical objective is to keep reducing p50 monotonically while keeping 4/4 correctness.
nextAction.expectedOutput: A measured p50 for the 3-launch path; if it lands near ~8-9us the launch-count model is confirmed and the next round should test a single-fused-kernel path (torch.compile guarded by an eager fallback) or a CUDA-graph replay of the same 3 ops, both of which collapse the remaining per-op dispatch cost.

risks: The accept-gate performance target (99.9999% improvement on a 15.36us baseline) is not reachable by any GPU kernel implementation; this candidate targets a real, measurable p50 reduction, not the literal target.
No local execution was performed this turn (per the mission rules), so the 3-launch gain is projected from round-1 launch-count evidence rather than measured.
If the shared runner's p50 is dominated by something other than per-op launch overhead (e.g. allocator or event-record cost), the improvement may be smaller than projected.

+_CONSTANTS = {}
+

+def _constants(x):
+    key = (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, x.device)
+    pair = _CONSTANTS.get(key)

-    # Initial implementation deliberately does one redundant device copy.
-    value = torch.relu(inputs['x'] * 1.25 + inputs['y'] * 0.75 - 0.125)
-    return value.clone()
+    x = inputs['x']
+    y = inputs['y']
+    ones, shift = _constants(x)
+    # 1.25*x + 0.75*y - 0.125 == 1.25*(x + 0.6*y) - 0.125.
+    # Folding the two input coefficients into one alpha-add removes a whole
+    # elementwise kernel, and the remaining scale (-1.25) plus shift (-0.125)
+    # are performed by a single addcmul before the in-place relu, so the whole
+    # operator is three kernel launches instead of four.  1.25 and 0.125 are
+    # exact in fp32; the only new rounding is the 0.6 alpha, which keeps the
+    # result far inside the 1e-5 atol/rtol budget.  inputs are never mutated.
+    combined = torch.add(x, y, alpha=0.6)
+    scaled = torch.addcmul(shift, combined, ones, value=1.25)
+    return scaled.relu_()
